newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-GRAF READY TO ADD TO GRAND SLAM HAUL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF READY TO ADD TO GRAND SLAM HAUL.

text.p: World number one Steffi Graf, unbeaten in her last six grand slam tournaments, declared herself fit and ready on Thursday to challenge for a fifth Australian Open title.
"I have practised a lot over the last few days and I am fit and ready," said Graf, the overwhelming favourite after the withdrawal of her main rival Monica Seles.
Graf missed the last two Australian Opens because of injury, leaving the path clear for Seles to win at Melbourne Park last year.

"For a couple of years I was not playing the Australian Open, now I'm back and she has got has got injured again," the 27-year-old German told reporters. "To miss a player of her status in a tournament is quite disappointing from the players' point of view."
Graf, whose season was badly disrupted because of injury last year, said she would deliberately cut her tournament workload in 1997.
"I am not pushing myself to play more," Graf said. "I am going to stick to the schedule that I had last year."
In the absence of Seles, who was forced to pull out because of a broken finger, Swiss teenager Martina Hingis has emerged as Graf's most serious challenger.
Unseeded last year, 16-year-old Hingis is seeded fourth and is the second favourite.
Graf herself sees the teenager as a major threat.

"She had an incredible year," said Graf. "Especially in the last few months, she seems not afraid of playing the top players and not afriad of winning tournaments. She's got an incredible mind on the court and she knows what to do."

A relaxed Graf showed none of the emotional and physical strain she felt in 1996, when her father, Peter, was remanded in a German jail on tax charges and a foot injury restricted her to 10 tournaments.
"I have not played a lot of tournaments, but the big tournaments I played extremely well for the time I was practising on the court," Graf said.
Asked if her goal was to remain number one, Graf replied emphatically, "No it's not."
"I play the tournaments I want and I do not care about the rankings."
